We are KARMA. AI and ML students from Bursa Technical University. 

Every member of our team is really into project and product development. We love testing ourselves with problem-solving in real life problems. Our goal is to implement ai/ml solutions to build smarter systems for a better future.
summary:
KARMA: Flame in Freefall is an interactive, zero-hallucination microgravity combustion analytics and mission safety platform built on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) archive. In microgravity and partial-gravity environments (such as Lunar habitats at 1/6g with elevated ~34% oxygen), buoyancy vanishes, transforming familiar teardrop flames into quiet, soot-free blue spheres that can spread unpredictably under cabin ventilation or smolder undetected.

Our platform bridges raw scientific data and mission-critical decisions by uniting four integrated capabilities: (1) an interactive Visual Story explaining buoyancy-to-diffusion physics; (2) a parametric Flame Lab simulating gravity, oxygen, pressure, airflow, and E-field ion-wind effects with explicit "Evidence Boundary" alerts whenever user inputs exceed tested NASA regimes; (3) an interactive 3D ISS Destiny Lab Fire & Telemetry Simulator visualizing real flight experiments (Saffire-I, BASS-II, FLEX, SAME-R); and (4) a Citation-Grounded Safety Analyst and Mission Ranker mapping 23 curated studies and 9 verified NASA CSV datasets to crew protocols and Earth fire-safety spin-offs.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Orbital Telemetry transforms NASA’s complex microgravity combustion archive into a unified web-based engineering and educational platform. Rather than treating scattered reports as static text, our system structures 23 curated study cards across 19 unique NASA PSI accessions and 9 experimental CSV datasets (671 source rows, 8,546 verified cells) with SHA-256 integrity verification and zero synthetic data imputation. Users explore fire behavior across five synchronized modules:

  1. Visual Story: Split-screen physics comparison contrasting Earth buoyancy-driven flames (1.0g) with diffusion-dominated microgravity flames (0g) and the Artemis Lunar Habitat elevated-oxygen paradox (30–34% O₂).
  2. Flame Lab: A real-time HTML5 Canvas fluid-advection and particle simulator allowing engineers to test gravity (0g–1.0g), oxygen (18%–36%), pressure (50–101.3 kPa), forced HVAC airflow (0–30 cm/s), fuel materials (PMMA, Cotton, Nomex, Heptane, Kapton), and DC electric fields (E-FIELD Flames ion wind).
  3. US Lab 3D Fire & Telemetry Sim: A Three.js WebGL reconstruction of the ISS Destiny laboratory module integrated with calibrated 3D flame visualization, sample tray positioning, and synchronized thermocouple/radiometer telemetry playback for Saffire-I, BASS-II, FLEX, and SAME-R.
  4. Mission & Data Ranker: A multi-criteria relevance engine that scores and ranks NASA PSI investigations according to mission profile (ISS, Lunar Habitat, Transit Spacecraft) and exports clean CSV matrices for predictive modeling.
  5. AI Safety Analyst & Earth Spin-Offs: A citation-grounded inquiry console linking every safety claim to verifiable PSI/NTRS identifiers, paired with an automated ISS Flight Rule 7.4.2 emergency checklist and a showcase of terrestrial spin-offs (fine water-mist suppression, optical cool-flame detectors, and lightweight composite firefighter gear).

Engineering & Scientific Integrity (Creative Approach): A key innovation of our platform is Scientific Honesty via Evidence Boundaries. In high-stakes aerospace engineering, unverified AI extrapolation is dangerous. Whenever a user simulates atmospheric conditions beyond NASA’s tested experimental envelope (such as untested combinations of high airflow and 35% O₂ in partial gravity), the simulator explicitly flags an Evidence Boundary Warning and recommends the exact next flight experiment needed to close that data gap.

Tools, Languages & Architecture: Built with vanilla ES Modules (JavaScript), HTML5 Canvas (2D fluid/particle physics), Three.js / WebGL (3D ISS Destiny lab environment), custom responsive CSS3, esbuild for production bundling, and Node.js automated test & SHA-256 data-integrity verification pipelines.
